seo_title: Cost of Living in Antalya 2026: Visa, Prices, Reviews | Relocost
seo_description: How much does it cost to live in Antalya per month, do Russians need a visa, work, rent and reviews from those who relocated. A realistic moving budget in the Relocost calculator.
intro_text: Visa-free entry for 90 days, mild winters, well-developed Russian-speaking infrastructure and affordable healthcare. A favourite city for families with children and those moving to the sea.
pros: Visa-free entry for 90 days, with the option to obtain a residence permit
Mild winters at +15°C and a 7-month swimming season
A large Russian-speaking community — schools, doctors, cafés
Direct flights from many Russian cities
cons: Hot summers at +35–40°C — tough without air conditioning
The Turkish lira is volatile — saving in TRY is risky
Difficulties with banks for Russians: opening an account has become harder

visa_steps.title: Visa-free entry
visa_steps.description: Up to 90 days within 180. A stamp at the border with a passport.

visa_steps.title: Residence permit via rental or property
visa_steps.description: A tourist ikamet for 1–2 years through a long-term lease or buying property from $200,000.

visa_steps.title: Tax number (Vergi numarası)
visa_steps.description: Issued at the tax office within a day — needed for an account and a rental.

visa_steps.title: Bank account
visa_steps.description: Ziraat, Denizbank, Kuveyt Türk — they work with Russians but require a residence permit or a tax number.

visa_steps.title: Address registration (Adres beyanı)
visa_steps.description: At the Nüfus office after getting the residence permit — for healthcare, school and services.

faq.question: Is Antalya suitable for families with children?
faq.answer: Yes, there are Russian private schools and kindergartens, healthcare such as Memorial Antalya, and affordable prices.

faq.question: What is healthcare like in Antalya?
faq.answer: World-class private clinics (Medical Park, Memorial); most procedures are cheaper than in the EU.

faq.question: Which district should I choose in Antalya?
faq.answer: Konyaaltı — beach and modern complexes; Lara — premium; Muratpaşa — the centre; Kepez — budget-friendly.

faq.question: Is it worth moving to Antalya in winter?
faq.answer: January–February is +12–15°C, occasionally rainy. It's warm, but comfortable swimming starts in May.

faq.question: How is it with the language in Antalya?
faq.answer: Turkish is the main language, but in the tourist zone people speak Russian and English.

faq.question: Is it hard to get a residence permit in Antalya?
faq.answer: Since 2023 Antalya has many closed districts (kapalı bölge) — you need to look for housing in open districts.

reviews.text: I bought an apartment in Konyaaltı and got a residence permit. Life by the sea, my daughter in an international school, and I moved my business here. The downside — the lira keeps jumping.
I opened a practice for a Russian-speaking audience — the demand is huge. Antalya is work and leisure at the same time.
